title: Types of migration

draft.title: Types of migration
card: a person moves to a new place and plans to stay there for good.
a person moves for a set time, such as to work or study, and then leaves or returns.
a person moves back and forth between places, such as a seasonal worker who goes to the same farms each year and then returns home.
a person has to leave because of war, persecution or disaster, and does not choose to go. Refugees are an example.
draft.remember: Types of migration differ in how long people stay and whether they choose to go.

a.q: Which type of migration is a refugee who flees a war?
a.why: A refugee leaves because of danger, not by choice, so this is forced migration. It may be tempting to call it permanent, but a refugee's move is described by the lack of choice, not by how long they stay.
a.clue: Did the person choose to leave?

b.q: Every winter, Tom lives in Broome for four months to work in a pearl shop, then returns to his home in Hobart. What type of migration is this?
b.why: Tom moves back and forth between the same two places in a regular pattern, so it is circular migration. It is not a one-off temporary move, because the trip repeats and he returns each time.
b.clue: Look at whether the move happens once or repeats.
